title: Flatness modulo all powers of an ideal implies flatness (Noetherian case)
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a ring map of commutative rings, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal and $M$ an $S$-module (an $R$-module via $\varphi$). Assume (1) $R$ is a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; (2) $S$ is a Noetherian ring; (3) $M$ is a finitely generated $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; (4) for every $n\ge1$ the module $M/I^nM$ is flat over $R/I^n$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then for every prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq S$ containing $IS$ (the ideal of $S$ generated by $\varphi(I)$) the localization $M_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a flat $R$-module. In particular, if $S$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_S$ and $IS\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, then $M$ is a flat $R$-module.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0523 (lemma-flat-module-powers, line 23807); its proof uses Lemma Tag 00ML (lemma-variant-local-criterion-flatness), Remark lemma-Tor-ring-mod-ideal and Lemma Tag 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module, Artin-Rees)

proof.text: Setup. Fix a prime $\mathfrak q\subset S$ with $IS\subseteq\mathfrak q$ and put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, a prime of $R$; since $\varphi(I)\subseteq IS\subseteq\mathfrak q$ we have $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Let $\mu:I\otimes_RM\to M$, $a\otimes m\mapsto\varphi(a)m$, and $K=\ker\mu$. Both $I\otimes_RM$ (through the factor $M$) and $M$ are $S$-modules and $\mu$ is $S$-linear, so $K$ is an $S$-submodule. For $n\ge1$ the image of $I^n\otimes_RM\to I\otimes_RM$ is $I^{n-1}(I\otimes_RM)$: $I^n$ is additively generated by products $ab$ with $a\in I^{n-1}$, $b\in I$, and $(ab)\otimes m=a\cdot(b\otimes m)$. Since $R$ acts on $I\otimes_RM$ through $\varphi$ and $S$, $I^{n-1}(I\otimes_RM)=(IS)^{n-1}(I\otimes_RM)$ as $S$-submodules.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0523 (lemma-flat-module-powers, line 23807)

proof.text: $K\subseteq I^{n-1}(I\otimes_RM)$ for every $n\ge1$. Fix $n$. Since $M/I^nM$ is flat over $R/I^n$ (hypothesis (4)) and $I/I^n\to R/I^n$ is injective, the map $I/I^n\otimes_{R/I^n}M/I^nM\to R/I^n\otimes_{R/I^n}M/I^nM=M/I^nM$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] (2) with $J=I^n$, $A=I/I^n$, $I/I^n\otimes_{R/I^n}M/I^nM\cong I/I^n\otimes_RM$; by right exactness [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] applied to $I^n\to I\to I/I^n\to0$ and the previous step, $I/I^n\otimes_RM\cong(I\otimes_RM)/I^{n-1}(I\otimes_RM)$. The composite $I\otimes_RM\to(I\otimes_RM)/I^{n-1}(I\otimes_RM)\cong I/I^n\otimes_{R/I^n}M/I^nM\to M/I^nM$ sends $a\otimes m$ to $am\bmod I^nM$, i.e. equals $I\otimes_RM\xrightarrow{\mu}M\to M/I^nM$. An element $k\in K$ maps to $0$ in $M$, so its image in $I/I^n\otimes_{R/I^n}M/I^nM$ maps to $0$ in $M/I^nM$, hence is $0$ by injectivity; thus $k\in I^{n-1}(I\otimes_RM)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0523 (lemma-flat-module-powers, line 23807)

proof.text: $K_{\mathfrak q}=0$ (Stacks: 'by the Artin-Rees lemma, and more precisely Lemma 00IQ'). $I$ is a finitely generated ideal, $I=(a_1,\dots,a_k)$, since $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $M$ is generated over $S$ by $m_1,\dots,m_l$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; as $a\otimes sm=s(a\otimes m)$, the elements $a_i\otimes m_j$ generate $N=I\otimes_RM$ as an $S$-module. By the previous steps $K\subseteq\bigcap_{k\ge0}(IS)^kN$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-localization] to the Noetherian ring $S$, the ideal $IS$, the finite $S$-module $N$ and the prime $\mathfrak q\supseteq IS$: there is $f\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that every element of $\bigcap_k(IS)^kN$, hence of $K$, is killed by a power of $f$. As $f^e\notin\mathfrak q$, every $x/t\in K_{\mathfrak q}$ is $0$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0523 (line 23840), using Lemma Tag 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module, line 12257) part (1)

proof.text: The multiplication $\mu':M_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_RI\to M_{\mathfrak q}$, $x\otimes a\mapsto\varphi(a)x$, is injective. Localization at $T=S\setminus\mathfrak q$ is exact [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]; applied to $0\to K\to I\otimes_RM\xrightarrow{\mu}M$ and $K_{\mathfrak q}=0$ it shows $\mu_{\mathfrak q}:(I\otimes_RM)_{\mathfrak q}\to M_{\mathfrak q}$ injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] (with $A=S$, the $S$-module $M$ and the $R$-module $I$, after the swap $I\otimes_RM\cong M\otimes_RI$) $(I\otimes_RM)_{\mathfrak q}\cong M_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_RI$ by $(a\otimes m)/t\mapsto(m/t)\otimes a$; on these generators $\mu_{\mathfrak q}$ gives $\varphi(a)m/t$ and $\mu'$ gives $\varphi(a)(m/t)$, the same, so $\mu'$ corresponds to $\mu_{\mathfrak q}$ and is injective.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0523 (line 23827: 'it suffices to check that Tor_1^R(M,R/I) is zero on localization at q'); the passage to R_p -> S_q needed to apply Lemma 00ML is implicit in Stacks and written out here, with Lemma Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization, line 9196) parts (1),(2)

proof.text: The local situation. For $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$, $\varphi(s)\notin\mathfrak q$, so $\varphi(s)$ is a unit of $S_{\mathfrak q}$ and acts invertibly on $M_{\mathfrak q}$; hence $\varphi$ induces $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}:R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$, $r/s\mapsto\varphi(r)/\varphi(s)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is an $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module through it, extending its $R$-module structure. $R_{\mathfrak p}$, $S_{\mathfrak q}$ are local with maximal ideals $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]; $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}(\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p})\subseteq\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ since $\varphi(\mathfrak p)\subseteq\mathfrak q$, so $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}$ is a local homomorphism. $J:=IR_{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ is a proper ideal since $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$. $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is generated over $S_{\mathfrak q}$ by the $m_j/1$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0523 (line 23827: 'it suffices to check that Tor_1^R(M,R/I) is zero on localization at q'); the passage to R_p -> S_q needed to apply Lemma 00ML is implicit in Stacks and written out here, with Lemma Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization, line 9196) parts (1),(2)

proof.text: $J\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}M_{\mathfrak q}\to M_{\mathfrak q}$ is injective (this is $\mathrm{Tor}_1^{R_{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak q},R_{\mathfrak p}/J)=0$ by Remark 00M6). $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is flat over $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], so $R_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_RI\to R_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_RR=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $y\otimes a\mapsto ya/1$, is injective [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; its image is $J$, so $R_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_RI\cong J$ as $R_{\mathfrak p}$-modules. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-cancel-base-change] (ring map $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$, the $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module $M_{\mathfrak q}$, the $R$-module $I$) $M_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}J\cong M_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}(R_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_RI)\cong M_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_RI$, $x\otimes(ya/1)\mapsto yx\otimes a$. Under this, the multiplication $x\otimes j\mapsto jx$ becomes $\mu'$ of step 4 (both give $\varphi(a)yx$ on $x\otimes(ya/1)$), which is injective.

proof.text: $M_{\mathfrak q}/JM_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R_{\mathfrak p}/J$. (a) $(M/IM)_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R/I$: let $u:N_1\to N_2$ be an injective map of $R/I$-modules. $M/IM$ is flat over $R/I$ (hypothesis (4), $n=1$), so $u\otimes1:N_1\otimes_{R/I}M/IM\to N_2\otimes_{R/I}M/IM$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; it is $S/IS$-linear, so its localization at the image of $S\setminus\mathfrak q$ is injective [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], and by the naturality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] (base ring $R/I$, $A=S/IS$) that localization is $u\otimes1:N_1\otimes_{R/I}(M/IM)_{\mathfrak q}\to N_2\otimes_{R/I}(M/IM)_{\mathfrak q}$. (b) Localizing the exact sequence $IM\to M\to M/IM\to0$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] gives $(M/IM)_{\mathfrak q}\cong M_{\mathfrak q}/I M_{\mathfrak q}=M_{\mathfrak q}/JM_{\mathfrak q}$, compatibly with the $R/I$-actions. (c) With $\bar{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak p/I$, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] gives $R_{\mathfrak p}/J\cong(R/I)_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}$, so $R/I\to R_{\mathfrak p}/J$ is a localization of $R/I$ at $(R/I)\setminus\bar{\mathfrak p}$; $M_{\mathfrak q}/JM_{\mathfrak q}$ is an $R_{\mathfrak p}/J$-module whose restricted $R/I$-structure is the one in (a),(b); by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] it is flat over $R_{\mathfrak p}/J$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0523 (line 23827: 'By assumption M/IM is flat over R/I'); localization step written out by the worker, cf. Lemma Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization) (2)

proof.text: By steps 5-7, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-variant-local-criterion] applies to the local homomorphism $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}:R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ of Noetherian local rings, the proper ideal $J$ and the finite $S_{\mathfrak q}$-module $M_{\mathfrak q}$: $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is a flat $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module. Since $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a localization at $R\setminus\mathfrak p$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] gives that $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is a flat $R$-module.

proof.text: The last clause. If $S$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_S\supseteq IS$, take $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak m_S$: every $t\in S\setminus\mathfrak m_S$ is a unit, so $M\to M_{\mathfrak m_S}$, $m\mapsto m/1$, is an $R$-linear bijection (inverse $m/t\mapsto t^{-1}m$), and $M$ is flat over $R$ because $M_{\mathfrak m_S}$ is [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].
